descriptions.index.html: Guide, recipes, samples and a needs catalogue for building custom retail POS apps, integrations and extensions on iVendNext without changing the product.
descriptions.start.html: Five steps from nothing to your first working call against an iVendNext sandbox: request a site, get the kit, make your app's user and key, run a sample.
descriptions.needs/index.html: What retailers ask for, in their own words, and whether you can build it on iVendNext today: the verdict, the door, the recipe and the limits to state.
descriptions.build.html: You know what you are building: the ladder of ways in, the recipe and sample for each rung, your sandbox and the tests that let an iVendNext app ship.
descriptions.plan.html: Plan an iVendNext project from a customer's list of needs to a release: tick the needs, get the order to build them in and the limits to put in the quote.
descriptions.sandbox.html: Request a sandbox: your own iVendNext site with made-up demo data, hosted by us, where you build and test before you touch a customer's site.
descriptions.publish.html: Publish your app to the iVendNext App library with one command from any computer, so retailers can find it and install it. We never take your source code.
descriptions.starters.html: Starting points for connecting a local ERP, payment gateway or wallet, loyalty provider, messaging gateway or delivery app to iVendNext.
descriptions.hosting.html: Run your app's service on iVendNext App Hosting or on your own cloud: the two side by side, who can host with CitiXsys, the plans, and the builder's journey.
descriptions.security.html: How a retailer and your app trust each other: its consent, your app's own user, the signed call and its check, rotation, and the till when your app is down.
descriptions.api.html: Every record call the kit's samples make to an iVendNext site: each address with its method, purpose, parameters, sign-in and answers, from the kit's API file.
descriptions.reference_apps.html: Working code to start from: samples that show one way into iVendNext with their tests, and reference apps that combine several, with the door each one uses.
descriptions.samples/index.html: Small working examples of each way into iVendNext, with their tests: pick the nearest to your project, run it against your sandbox and change it.
descriptions.recipes/index.html: One recipe for each job on iVendNext: what it does, who it is for, the steps with their commands, and what iVendNext refuses.
descriptions.guide/03_ladder_and_never_list.html: The ladder is the order to try the ways into iVendNext, from settings to your own service, and the four rules every project keeps. Read it before each project.
descriptions.guide/04_configure_first.html: Most of what a retailer asks for is already a setting in iVendNext Desk. See what to set up before you write any code, so the need stops at the first rung.
descriptions.guide/09_points_and_requests.html: What an extension point is, which ones iVendNext publishes, and how to ask for a new one when no rung of the ladder fits the customer's need.
descriptions.guide/16_possible_not_possible.html: A straight answer to 'can we do this for the customer?' before you quote: what is possible today, what is not yet, what never, and the limits for each.
descriptions.recipes/connected_app.html: Build a connected app: your service, in any language, on its own server, that reads and writes a retailer's iVendNext over the record API. Steps and commands.
descriptions.recipes/configure_no_code.html: Set iVendNext up with no code: coded reasons, IMEI tracking, one more detail per line and member pricing, using only what iVendNext already has.
descriptions.recipes/till_guard.html: Put several till rules in one app, with settings the retailer edits in Desk: a manager for a large sale, a most-per-line quantity, a beep on a flagged item.
descriptions.recipes/manifest.html: Ship your own record types and fields to a retailer's iVendNext in one manifest file, without code inside it: bins, warranty terms, a reference list.
descriptions.recipes/rule_guard.html: Check a sale before payment: your service allows it, refuses it in your own words, or asks the cashier a yes or no question when Pay is pressed.
descriptions.recipes/capture.html: Capture a value at the scan, or send a one-time code before a new customer is added: your HTTPS service answers at a moment the cashier did not choose.
